transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-18
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Summit Health - Head of ML Ops), Tom Blake (Platform Eng), Sofia Chen (Procurement), Ben Ortiz (SRE)

Summary: quick renewal + expansion checkin to confirm capacity upgrade, additional region onboarding, and contract extension timeline. Discussed latency targets, data residency, and procurement steps. Action items and follow-ups captured.

[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, hope you can hear me ok. we got about 45 minutes, main goal is to lock scope for the renewal and the extra region request and make sure the procurement timing lines up.
[00:12] Aisha Rahman: yeah sounds good, thanks Lena. we'll probably hand this over to Sofia for contract but i wanted to be clear on capacity numbers and perf.
[00:20] Marco Diaz: hi all, Marco here — i'll cover the technical bits, benchmarks, and what Dedicated looks like in practice.
[00:26] Tom Blake: hey, quick note that Ben's joining for the VPC/KMS bits so if we dig into networking he'll chime in.
[00:32] Ben Ortiz: yep thanks Tom, i'll jump in on any network or infra questions.

[00:40] Lena Park: to recap from the renewal thread — you're on our hosted plan, average tokens per month ~ 650M, peak p95 latency right now around 420ms for the chat flows, correct?
[00:50] Aisha Rahman: that's about right. peak is spiky during batch inference overnight but daytime p95 is what matters for user-facing. cost is creeping up with recent feature rollouts.
[01:03] Marco Diaz: we've looked at your telemetry — the usage pattern is very bursty, which makes a good case for reserved capacity plus autoscale. Dedicated will give predictable throughput and lower per-token cost for sustained bursts.
[01:15] Aisha Rahman: curious about the cost delta — we ran a quick calc vs Anthropic endpoints and our internal infra; can you share an apples-to-apples?
[01:24] Lena Park: yes, i'll send a pricing comparison. short answer: Dedicated reduces unit cost at scale and gives cost predictability — but there's upfront commit. we'll put together a region-by-region estimate in the doc.

[01:36] Tom Blake: we also have a compliance ask: the new regulation requires data to be in-region for EU customers. we need an extra EU region for inference, preferably FRA or AMS. how fast do you stand up a new region on Dedicated?
[01:50] Marco Diaz: for Dedicated we can provision in an EU region within 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and infra partner availability. for Private (VPC) it depends on customer infra readiness — typically 3-6 weeks. note: there may be an additional setup fee.
[02:05] Ben Ortiz: and for KMS — we need support for customer-managed keys (HSM-backed KMS). does Redwood support that in Dedicated?
[02:12] Marco Diaz: yes, KMS integrations are supported — we have both cloud KMS and HSM options for Private deployments; on Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS via mTLS and key wrap. i'll share the integration doc.

[02:25] Sofia Chen: procurement note — we'll need a sample SLA and the security pack (SOC2, ISO certs, pen test docs). also can you lock in pricing for 12 months?
[02:35] Lena Park: absolutely. we'll draft a 12-month addendum with reserved capacity terms and include the compliance bundle.
[02:41] Aisha Rahman: good. about performance — Marco, can you walk us through latency improvements if we add an EU region and move some traffic there? and how does autoscaling burst work?
[02:52] Marco Diaz: sure. moving traffic to a closer region reduces network RTT; for your p95 we estimate ~100-150ms improvement for EU traffic. autoscaling for Dedicated uses a warm pool and fast spin-up; bursts are handled by reserved GPUs plus ephemeral burst capacity if enabled. we also recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts to cut token generation by 10-20% effectively.
[03:12] Tom Blake: what about model variants — we sometimes need to fallback to a smaller quantized model during overload to preserve latency. is that supported?
[03:20] Marco Diaz: yes, smart routing supports model variants for graceful degradation. you can configure policy to route to cheaper/quantized model on high load. logs and tracing will show which variant served each request.

[03:32] Aisha Rahman: we like that. can you run a benchmark with our prompt set — 100 concurrent sessions, mixed-length tokens — to validate latency under load before we commit?
[03:41] Lena Park: yes, Marco will run the sim and share results.
[03:44] Marco Diaz: i'll need the prompt set and a sample traffic profile. if you can drop those in the shared drive i'll run the 10k token/hour sim and a 3-hour stress test. 
[03:55] Sofia Chen: timeline for procurement — we need pricing and a PO-ready quote by early next week to hit our finance cycle. is that realistic?
[04:03] Lena Park: we can get a draft quote by Friday — final contract may depend on legal redlines.
[04:08] Sofia Chen: ok thanks. also we occasionally evaluate Google Cloud AI — any interoperability with GCP infra for peering?
[04:16] Marco Diaz: yes, we can peer with GCP and other cloud providers; Dedicated supports cross-cloud routing and VPC peering. note: cross-cloud egress may affect cost.

[04:28] Ben Ortiz: small note on monitoring — we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards available in console. can those be retained for 6 months?
[04:38] Marco Diaz: retention is configurable; standard is 30 days, but we can add extended retention as an add-on for 6-12 months. we'll include that in the pricing sheet.

[04:49] Aisha Rahman: any blockers you see for us moving to Dedicated + EU region?
[04:54] Marco Diaz: main blockers are: 1) VPC peering approvals on your side, 2) KMS/HSM negotiations, and 3) procurement signoff for commit. technically it's straightforward.
[05:03] Lena Park: to summarize next steps — Marco runs the benchmark (due Thu), Lena will send updated pricing and sample SLA (due Fri), Aisha/Sofia confirm regions and procurement timeline (due Aug 25), and we'll tentatively schedule pilot kickoff week of Aug 29. does that sound right?
[05:17] Aisha Rahman: yes that's good.
[05:19] Sofia Chen: agreed. thank you.
[05:21] Tom Blake: one last quick question — if we need private (on-prem) for some clients, what's the delta in onboarding time vs Dedicated?
[05:29] Marco Diaz: on-prem is more variable; typical onboarding 6-12 weeks due to network and infra approvals, air-gap considerations, and KMS. Dedicated is the faster path.

[05:40] Lena Park: perfect, we'll follow up with the docs and pricing. thanks everyone for the time.
[05:46] Ben Ortiz: thanks all.

Recap & links:
- Benchmark prompt set: link to shared drive (customer provided)
- Pricing draft (to be attached by Lena)
- Security pack & SOC2 certs (link to Redwood security page)

End of transcript
